title: Life sciences firm Danaher to launch AI-powered autonomous research lab in 2027
source_used: Healthcare Digital (original Reuters item blocked here: HTTP 401)
key_facts: Danaher, a life sciences firm, announced plans for its first AI-powered autonomous lab, expected to become operational in early 2027.
The lab is based at Danaher company Abcam in Cambridge, UK, and will use AI to design affinity reagents, including antibodies, then build and test each candidate automatically.
The lab combines technologies from Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies and Molecular Devices; robotic automation was developed with Automata.
Danaher CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery says the lab will help researchers move from an idea to tested and validated affinity reagents up to 8 times faster.
Luciano Lucas, Vice President and Enterprise Head of Autonomous and Intelligent Labs at Danaher, says the lab could benefit scientists in manual, semi-automated or fully autonomous environments.
quote_evidence: Expected to become operational in early 2027, the lab will fuse AI, robotics and various Danaher technologies into a single workflow to help researchers rapidly develop custom antibodies and molecular tools.
Danaher CEO Julie Sawyer Montgomery says the lab will help "researchers move from an idea to tested and validated affinity reagents up to 8x faster while maintaining scientific rigour."
These capabilities can benefit scientists whether they work in manual, semi-automated, or fully autonomous environments.
why_it_matters_hint: A large life sciences company is building an automated AI lab for making research tools, which could speed up drug discovery if the claims hold.
notes: Healthcare Digital does not name a source; its quotes come from Danaher's own announcement. Reuters carries the same news (blocked here). The 8x speed claim is the company's, attributed in the entry. Pool score kept at 6.
